owis.original: उपाधींत सांपडों नये । उपाधीस कंटाळों नये । निसुगपण कामा नये । कोणीयेकविषीं ॥ २० ॥
owis.marathiMeaning: महंतानें उपाधींत अडकूं नये तरी उपाधीला कंटाळू नये. कोणत्याही कामाबद्दल त्यानें आळस दाखवतां कामा नये.
owis.englishMeaning: That atma should not be found in this limiting concept of a gross body; that atma should not be wearied by this limiting concept; that One who is within everyone should have no desire for laziness.

owis.original: काम नासणार नासतें । आपण वेडें उगें च पाहातें । आळसी हृदयसून्य तें । काये करुं जाणे ॥ २१ ॥
owis.marathiMeaning: आळशीपणा केल्यानें कार्याचा नाश व्हायचा तो होतोच, व वेडेपणानें हा उगीच त्याच्याकडे पहात राहतो. हृदयशून्य व आळशी असा तो त्याबाबतींत कांहीं करुं शकत नाहीं.
owis.englishMeaning: When you feel that there is something that needs to be done then, that One who does not do, gets spoiled. For you have been enamoured by this world and then that still and silent Self regards this world only. How can the lazy make and know this *zero and that Reality? (You are that still and silent Reality and in that Reality there is complete contentment and nothing needs to be done. But you have forgotten your Self and that contentment and run around the world looking for that which is already with you) *(When nothing is there, everything is there ie. knowledge)

owis.original: धकाधकीचा मामला । कैसा घडे अशक्ताला । नाना बुद्धि शक्ताला । म्हणोनी सिकवाव्या ॥ २२ ॥
owis.marathiMeaning: महंताचें जीवन म्हणजे धकाधकीचा व्यवहार आहे. देहानें व मनानें व वृत्तीनें जो अशक्त आहे, त्याला तो जमत नाहीं. म्हणून जो शरीरानें व मनानें बलवान आहे, त्याला नाना प्रकारच्या युक्त्या, विचार आणि कौशल्य शिकवावे.
owis.englishMeaning: Where there are toils and vexations then, what can that weak and incompetent buddhi accomplish? The buddhi of the `many' therefore, should be taught this power of `I am'.

owis.original: व्याप होईल तों राहावें । व्याप राहातां उठोन जावें । आनंदरुप फिरावें । कोठे तर्‍ही ॥ २३ ॥
owis.marathiMeaning: कार्याचा व्याप आपण जोपर्यंत सांभाळू शकतो, तोपर्यंत लोकसमुदायांत राहावें. तें अशक्य झालें कीं, तेथून चालते व्हावें. मगआनंदानें कोठेतरी परिभ्रमण करीत फिरावें.
owis.englishMeaning: When this power is pervasive then that atma can stay as the `all'. Now you have to awake from your pervasiveness and go away (you have awoken from the first dream now awake from this second dream of `I am knowledge' and don't exist). Then wherever He wanders, He moves in this bliss-form.

owis.original: उपाधीपासुनी सुटला । तो निस्पृहपणें बळावला । जिकडे अनुकूळ तिकडे चालिला । सावकास ॥ २४ ॥
owis.marathiMeaning: जो उपाधींतून मोकळा होतो, त्याची निःस्पृहता बळकट होते. मग त्याला ज्या ठिकाणीं अनुकूल परिस्थिती असेल तेथें तो स्वस्थपणें जाऊं शकतो.
owis.englishMeaning: That atma should be disconnected from this limiting concept by the powerful force of desirelessness. This `I am' only should do that which comes its way and have no desire for anything else. (Whatever comes is perfect, I am knowledge and I want to just completely know that which comes my way).

owis.original: कीर्ति पाहातां सुख नाहीं । सुख पाहातां कीर्ति नाहीं । केल्याविण कांहींच नाहीं । कोठें तर्‍ही ॥ २५ ॥
owis.marathiMeaning: कीर्ति पाहिजे असेल तर सुखासीनता चलणार नाहीं. आणि सुखासीनता हवी असेल तर कीर्ति मिळणार नाहीं. माणूस कोठेंही जावो, आपण केल्यावाचून कार्य घडत नाहीं. असेंच आढळते.
owis.englishMeaning: When you understand this pervasiveness then, there is no pleasure; and when you understand pleasure then, there is no pervasiveness (ie. there is a buddhi who wants this and that). If pervasiveness is not created then, this `thing' cannot be found.

owis.original: येरवीं काय राहातें । होणार तितुकें होऊन जातें । प्राणी मात्र अशक्त तें । पुढें आहे ॥ २६ ॥
owis.marathiMeaning: आपण केलें नाहीं तर कार्य अडून राहतें असें नाहीं. जें होणार असतें तें होऊन जाते. शक्तिहीन व बलहीन माणूसमात्र निमित्याला शोधत असतो.
owis.englishMeaning: How to stay effortlessly? Whatever is going to be, let that much happen and then let it go away (don't cover over that which is actually appearing with your minds thoughts). But if that Reality stays in only the prana, then it will become weak and have an incompetent buddhi.

owis.original: आधींच तकवा सोडिला । मधेंचि धीवसा सांडिला । तरी संसार हा सेवटाला । कैसा पावे ॥ २७ ॥
owis.marathiMeaning: संसार करतांना आधींच उत्साह सोडला किंवा मधेंच धीर सुटला, तर संसार शेवटपर्यंत निभावणें कठीण आहे.
owis.englishMeaning: If you thrown out this power and support of the source, then, in this worldly existence, fortitude and patience slip away. And tell me, how can thoughtlessness ever be acquired through samsar?

owis.original: संसार मुळींच नासका । विवेकें करावा नेटका । नेटका करितां फिका । होत जातो ॥ २८ ॥
owis.marathiMeaning: संसार हा मुळांतच नासका आहे. अशाश्वत आहे. विवेकाच्या सामर्थ्यानें तो व्यवस्थित करावा. असा तो व्यवस्थित केला तर त्याचा रस फिका होत जातो. त्याची आसक्ती क्षीण होत जाते.
owis.englishMeaning: samsar is the spoiling of this root (purush/prakruti). But by vivek, samsar is made right and proper (ie. becomes knowledge). But even by making it right and proper still it fades and goes away (ie. when you sleep or die, knowledge goes off; maharaj- sleep is a small death).

owis.original: ऐसा याचा जिनसाना । पाहातां कळों येतें मना । परंतु धीर सांडावाना । कोणीयेकें ॥ २९ ॥
owis.marathiMeaning: संसाराचा मालमसाला हा असा अशाश्वत आहे. त्याचे नीट निरीक्षण केलें कीं हे समजते. पटते. हे जरी खरें असलें तरी धीर सोडूं नये.
owis.englishMeaning: This most superior `object' of that witnessing purush has become like this. But if you truly understand your mind then, that Reality can be understood (when prakruti goes off then that purush who was intimately attached to her becomes that Reality). But that One who is within everyone should not leave His courage and steadfastness.

owis.original: धीर सांडितां काये होतें । अवघें सोसावें लागतें । नाना बुद्धि नाना मतें । शाहाणा जाणे ॥ ३० ॥
owis.marathiMeaning: धीर सोडल्यानें कांहीं फायदा होत नाहीं. माणसाला जें सोसयचे असेल तें सोसावे लागतेच. नाना प्रकारचे विचार व नाना प्रकारची मतें शहाणा जाणतो.
owis.englishMeaning: When courage and steadiness are left aside then, so much appears (ie. a whole world of ideas and concepts) and the `many' things have to be endured. But the wise know this buddhi of the `many' and its `many' opinions. .
